claims.statement: Einstein’s kinematic argument uses a relativity principle, invariant vacuum light speed and clock synchronization to derive frame-dependent distant simultaneity.
source_locators: Introduction; §§1–3
alternative_explanations: A preferred metaphysical frame requires added structure beyond the inspected formulation.
limitations: Reliable theoretical attribution, not a newly reviewed experiment or proof of a unique ontology.
claims.epistemic_scope: Attribution of an inspected theoretical construction, not an observed event or empirical confirmation.

claims.statement: Einstein’s §3 transformation and §4 moving-clock relation retain elapsed clock readings; unequal rates do not eliminate temporal succession.
source_locators: §3 final transformation; §4 moving clock at x=vt
alternative_explanations: Additional ontology may interpret the same measured relations differently.
limitations: Sub-luminal inertial-motion domain; no modern precision test audited.

claims.statement: In the displayed Lorentz relation, positive elapsed time along x=vt remains positive for |v|<c; a complete-history representation therefore need not collapse ordered clock events into one simultaneous event.
source_locators: §§3–4; author deduction in report
alternative_explanations: Whether all represented events equally exist is an additional metaphysical issue.
limitations: Conditional scope; does not establish actual timeless consciousness.

claims.statement: Rovelli distinguishes measurable partial observables from predictive complete correlations and treats physical clocks relationally.
source_locators: §II pendulum example; §III equation(4); §V equation(5)
limitations: Attribution of this formalism’s interpretation; not a measurement of foundational consciousness.
claims.epistemic_scope: Attribution of an inspected theoretical construction, not an observed event or empirical confirmation.

claims.statement: Rovelli’s constrained formulation does not require privileged external time; §VI explicitly restricts its detailed development to finite degrees of freedom while retaining histories and relational predictions.
source_locators: §VI opening; equations(6)–(11),(21)–(22); §VII
limitations: A theoretical framework, not an empirically confirmed complete quantum-gravity cosmology.
claims.epistemic_scope: Attribution of an inspected theoretical construction, not an observed event or empirical confirmation.

claims.statement: Neither coordinate-invariant observables nor omission of privileged external time entails absence of physical change, experience, or all intrinsic succession.
source_locators: §V equation(5) and clock example; §VII; author bridge assessment
alternative_explanations: A further ontology could posit a timeless foundation, but would need independent justification.
limitations: Conditional scope; does not establish actual timeless consciousness.

claims.statement: In Boethius V.6, Philosophy contrasts whole possession of life with endless sequential existence and places divine priority in simplicity rather than earlier duration.
source_locators: V.6 opening eternity/everlasting comparison
limitations: Historical argument attribution; “single moment” in this translation is read with its explicit contrast to temporal succession, not as a coordinate instant.

claims.statement: Boethius IV.6 distinguishes unified providence from its temporal unfolding; V.6 distinguishes conditional from simple necessity in replying to the foreknowledge objection.
source_locators: IV.6 providence/fate distinction; V.3 objection; V.6 knowledge/necessity reply
alternative_explanations: The account still owes an adequate relation between infallible knowledge, grounding and free choices.
limitations: Argument attribution, not an established solution to freedom, evil or providential action.

claims.statement: Craig’s tensed-fact objection is conditional on objective A-theoretic tense and a knower’s need to know what is presently true; he explicitly says a B-theory avoids this argument.
source_locators: Opening numbered argument; paragraph beginning The B-theorist; conclusion
alternative_explanations: Deny irreducible tensed facts or defend atemporal knowledge of them.
limitations: The disputed semantics and knowledge premise are not proven by the existence of a temporal world alone.

claims.statement: Craig argues that replacing propositional beliefs with direct intuition does not by itself remove the objection if irreducibly tensed reality still must be known.
source_locators: Omniscience Despite Ignorance of Tensed Facts; arguments4′ and4*
alternative_explanations: A defender can instead reject absolute presentness or justify a distinct access relation.
limitations: Craig’s objection is directly inspected; his accounts of modern defenders are not substitutes for their originals.

claims.statement: Craig’s personhood defense focuses on a God without temporal creation, distinguishing possible changeless self-awareness from interaction with temporal persons.
source_locators: Opening scope; Criteria Based on States of Consciousness
limitations: Possible personhood without creation is not proof of timeless responsiveness in the actual world.

claims.statement: Craig defends timeless volition by disputing that every intention is future-directed or reached by deliberation; the response invokes a possible unchanging will.
source_locators: Criteria Based on Intentionality
alternative_explanations: A critic may require agency to involve action or reasons responsive capacities whose timeless realization is still unexplained.
limitations: Counterexamples within temporal human life do not by themselves exhibit an actually timeless agent.

claims.statement: Craig also presents a model timeless without creation and temporal with creation; it is a temporal alternative once a world exists, not foundation-level H-T throughout that relation.
source_locators: States of Consciousness, Ockhamist model paragraphs; Inter-personal Relations
alternative_explanations: An atemporal foundation can instead deny the need for intrinsic change upon creating.
limitations: Explaining the relation without a literal temporal “before time” remains necessary; no cosmic clock identification adopted.

claims.statement: A conditional M2 model can posit one non-successive act that knows and grounds a temporally ordered history, provided the grounding relation and individuated subjectivity are independently intelligible.
source_locators: IV.6/V.6; Craig scope; author reconstruction in report
alternative_explanations: An impersonal relational structure or a temporal conscious foundation could realize comparable physical history.
limitations: Project reconstruction, not either source’s verbatim model or proof of full metaphysical coherence.

claims.statement: Knowing a dated event and each person’s indexical belief need not mean being that person or successively acquiring those beliefs; whether this exhausts knowledge of objective presentness is disputed.
source_locators: Craig tensed-fact sections; personhood self-consciousness passage; author reconstruction
alternative_explanations: A-theoretic presentness may demand a genuinely changing cognitive relation.
limitations: Conditional scope; does not establish actual timeless consciousness.

claims.statement: A changing time-indexed relation to a fixed foundation is distinct from a new intrinsic state of that foundation; the claim that every genuine response needs such a new state requires argument.
source_locators: IV.6; Inter-personal Relations; author reconstruction
alternative_explanations: Responsiveness understood as new awareness or deliberative revision entails succession.
limitations: Counterfactual dependence across possible histories is not a sequence of changes within one foundation.

claims.statement: M1 temporal continuation, M2 a timeless foundation with temporal persons, and M3 complete-history inclusion are distinct; inclusion of a finite life or its record alone does not meet H-S.
source_locators: T01 report §4; author mapping in report
alternative_explanations: A richer M3 must specify same-person subjectivity beyond the bodily-life boundary.
limitations: Internal conceptual inference under T01; personal identity adjudication deferred to T13.

claims.statement: Relativity, a relational formalism and eternalism do not alone identify an experiential bearer or the grounding relation needed for H-F, H-U, H-T or human survival.
source_locators: Kinematic/formalism scope; author argument A-T11-001
alternative_explanations: Independent philosophical arguments could supply a bridge; these physical formalisms do not supply it by themselves.
limitations: Conditional scope; does not establish actual timeless consciousness.

claims.statement: If rival metaphysical models yield the same physical and report predictions, those observations cannot distinguish them; a discriminating test requires independently specified differing expectations.
source_locators: Author discrimination analysis; reviewed T08/T09 report boundaries
alternative_explanations: A specified interaction model might predict additional measurable differences.
limitations: No assertion that all possible timeless and temporal models are empirically equivalent.

claims.statement: The Boethian and Craig discussions share premises about knowledge and personhood; they are not independent observations, and conditional coherence does not establish actuality or equal support for alternatives.
source_locators: Author dependence and sensitivity analysis
alternative_explanations: Additional independent evidence may change comparative support.
limitations: No quantitative metaphysical posterior or cumulative nine-component verdict.

arguments.name: Physical time without a metaphysical shortcut
premises: Rovelli’s histories and relational predictions survive removal of privileged external time.
bridge_principles: A formal representation does not determine the full ontology of what it represents.
arguments.conclusion: These results do not establish a timeless conscious bearer.
arguments.strongest_objection: An all-history representation may naturally motivate eternalist ontology.
arguments.strongest_reply: Even eternalism contains earlier/later relations and does not identify a single experiencing mind.
unresolved_issues: Interpretative merits of eternalism and rival ontologies remain open.
No broad quantum-gravity or empirical-relativity review.

arguments.name: A timeless conscious foundation with temporal manifestation
premises: Suppose a conscious ground can know ordered contents in one non-discursive act.
Suppose a non-temporal grounding relation can explain why a concrete history obtains.
Suppose individual perspectives are grounded without requiring additions to the ground.
bridge_principles: Explanatory and intentional priority need not be temporal priority.
A timeless intention can be directed toward a whole history and its ends.
arguments.conclusion: Under these substantive assumptions M2 avoids the simple accumulation contradiction and could unify temporal order with conscious grounding.
arguments.strongest_objection: The model may redescribe history without explaining its concrete existence or subjective individuation; a fixed act may not count as agency.
arguments.strongest_reply: It posits an actual subject and reasons-guided dependence, rather than merely an abstract record; the absence of deliberation does not by definition exclude intention.
unresolved_issues: Prove the proposed grounding relation intelligible and explanatory.
Supply comparative reason to prefer mind over impersonal structure.
Value and goodness require separate premises.

arguments.name: The tensed-knowledge challenge
premises: Suppose perfect knowledge must encompass which events are presently occurring.
Suppose tracking these changing truths requires intrinsic cognitive succession.
bridge_principles: The presence of irreducibly tensed reality, not mere temporal order, drives the inference.
arguments.conclusion: Then a cognitively perfect ground of this temporal world cannot meet H-T.
arguments.strongest_objection: A defender denies absolute presentness or argues one atemporal act knows every tensed fact through a non-successive access relation.
arguments.strongest_reply: The first response rejects a key premise and is a serious alternative; the second must explain access without either missing changing actuality or collapsing all times into one temporal present.
unresolved_issues: Neither A-theory nor B-theory settled here.
Direct modern defender originals and response chain remain coverage gaps.
Propositional and non-propositional knowledge need separate accounts.

arguments.name: Timeless personhood and intentional responsiveness
premises: Necessary conditions of personhood must not be inferred solely from the way finite humans learn.
A possible knower may have self-awareness and rational volition without deliberative updating.
Responsiveness can be specified as dependence of effects on reasons, or as newly acquired awareness; these differ.
bridge_principles: A capacity can remain unexercised; possible temporal exercise does not show the bearer already has succession.
arguments.conclusion: Simple personhood arguments do not automatically refute timelessness; actual interaction still needs a model.
arguments.strongest_objection: The proposed timeless capacities may be nominal; responsiveness to genuinely new events seems to require new states.
arguments.strongest_reply: Either justify whole-history reasons-sensitive dependence, or accept a temporal divine life with creation. Neither option is cost-free.
unresolved_issues: Transition into time must not posit a time before time.
Trinitarian illustration is an additional theological assumption, not universal-subject evidence.

arguments.name: Whole-history preservation versus survival
premises: Representing or including all events of a finite life preserves specified contents.
T01 H-S requires the same person’s subjectivity beyond irreversible bodily death.
bridge_principles: A record or a containing knower is not automatically numerically identical to the represented person.
arguments.conclusion: M3 inclusion alone supplies a preservation proposal, not H-S.
arguments.strongest_objection: An enlarged subject-history might include genuinely continuing subjectivity outside embodied succession.
arguments.strongest_reply: That is a distinct stronger hypothesis deserving assessment under an explicit identity relation; merely calling it inclusion does not establish it.
unresolved_issues: T13: bearer, death condition, numerical identity, continuation domain, memory and branching.

Original German and modern experimental tests not inspected. Not a full electrodynamics audit.

sources.title: The Consolation of Philosophy
sources.source_type: original philosophical text in historical English translation
relevant_locators: Title and preface; IV.6; V.3–6, especially V.6; translator note [S]
sources.provenance_notes: H. R. James 1897 translation, preface identifies Peiper 1874 Latin text. Inspected relevant prose and context, not the whole book or Latin manuscripts. Arguments voiced by Philosophy in a dialogue. Translation date distinct from ancient composition. Modern apparatus and poem are not treated as independent philosophical evidence. Translator note [S] disputes the text’s historical attribution to Plato; no independent Plato attribution adopted.

sources.title: Omniscience, Tensed Facts, and Divine Eternity
relevant_locators: Opening numbered argument and B-theory paragraph; Timeless Knowledge of Tensed Facts; Omniscience Despite Ignorance of Tensed Facts; Must God Be Omniscient?; notes1–44
sources.provenance_notes: Author-hosted body and references inspected. Exact publication/reprint date absent from inspected HTML; repository search metadata attributes April 2000, not independently checked journal edition. Core text is treated as a pre-cutoff historical argument; footer date is not publication date. Failed repository/PDF routes logged. Craig’s summaries of Kvanvig, Wierenga and Leftow do not count as inspecting those originals. No blanket endorsement of his criticisms.
